cta: Explore Fluxknight and see how Maia approaches customer support.
hook: When customers ask the same five questions every day, the problem is usually not employee performance—it is missing support structure.
title: Support teams should not answer the same question from memory

scenes.voiceover: When customers ask the same five questions every day, the problem is usually not employee performance—it is missing support structure.
scenes.on_screen_text: Same questions. Every day.\nThe problem is support structure.
scenes.visual_direction: Open on a near-black background with five violet-and-white enquiry cards rapidly stacking: “Availability?”, “Pricing?”, “How do I book?”, “Which documents?”, “Opening hours?” Add a subtle alert pulse and quick zoom toward the overloaded support inbox. Use premium white sans-serif typography and the Fluxknight purple accent.

scenes.voiceover: Each answer feels small. Together, they interrupt deeper work and make response quality depend on who is online.
scenes.visual_direction: Show a Fluxknight-style support workspace with incoming enquiry cards appearing over a task board. A human operator’s task cards dim as repeat questions cover the interface. Keep the UI illustrative and clearly framed as a workflow scenario, not a historical performance claim.

scenes.voiceover: The first useful automation step is not replacing the support team.
scenes.visual_direction: Transition to a clean workflow diagram on black: “Customer enquiry” flows into two violet branches labeled “Defined question” and “Needs judgment.” Animate the split with a crisp violet line and restrained glow.

scenes.voiceover: Maia can handle defined questions, such as availability, pricing, booking steps, documents, and opening hours.
scenes.visual_direction: Show a polished simulated Maia interface. A customer message enters: “Is the property available, and what documents do I need?” Maia highlights the defined topics, retrieves approved answer blocks, and displays a concise response preview. Include subtle “Configured answer” labels to clarify that the business controls the information.

scenes.voiceover: It can also collect the relevant details before the next step.
scenes.visual_direction: Animate a structured capture panel beside the conversation with fields such as “Enquiry type,” “Preferred date,” “Customer name,” and “Contact details.” Fields populate one at a time, with a violet completion indicator. Avoid presenting any invented customer data as a real result.

scenes.voiceover: And when a request needs judgment, Maia directs it to the right person instead of guessing.
scenes.on_screen_text: Repeatable information → Maia\nHuman decisions → Your team
scenes.visual_direction: Show an exception message: “Request needs review.” The workflow routes it from Maia to a human-assignee card labeled “Support team,” with a visible handoff status and conversation context attached. Use a clean animated connector and a human-review icon.

scenes.voiceover: Good support automation creates a clearer boundary between repeatable information and human decisions.
scenes.visual_direction: Pull back to the complete workflow: enquiry, Maia response, detail capture, human handoff. Add a restrained Fluxknight wordmark lockup with the X highlighted in violet. Keep the background black and the composition spacious.

objective: Educate operators that practical support automation separates predictable enquiries from cases requiring human judgment, while introducing Maia’s structured customer-support workflow.
